Incident Postmortem INC-2041 — Halvard Systems, ledger-api
Service: ledger-api (invoice rendering and retrieval for the Pelican Ledger product)
Date of incident: Tuesday 14 July 2026
Author: Dana Okafor (on-call engineer). Reviewers: Marcus Lindqvist (database lead), Ravi Thandeka (platform), Lena Baxter (support lead). Review meeting held Tuesday 21 July 2026.
Final severity: SEV1. Customer impact band: Medium. Data loss: none.

Severity table (reproduced from the Halvard incident policy)
- SEV3: partial degradation of any endpoint lasting under 15 minutes, or a complete outage lasting under 5 minutes.
- SEV2: partial degradation lasting between 15 and 60 minutes.
- SEV1: any complete outage lasting 5 minutes or more, or partial degradation lasting more than 60 minutes.
Customer impact bands: Low = fewer than 5% of active accounts affected; Medium = 5% to 25% of active accounts; High = more than 25% of active accounts.

Summary
Between 09:26 and 10:37 UTC on 14 July 2026, requests to the /invoices/render endpoint of ledger-api failed or timed out at an elevated rate, peaking at 38% of requests to that endpoint. All other endpoints, including invoice creation, invoice listing and payment webhooks, were unaffected throughout. The degradation was introduced by the deployment of ledger-api build 4.18.0, which shipped database migration 0472. The migration added an index on invoice_lines(invoice_id, position). Because the planner statistics for the table were stale, the query planner began choosing a sequential scan over the 41-million-row invoice_lines table for the render query. Service was restored by rolling back to build 4.17.3. No data was lost or corrupted.

Timeline (all times UTC)
- 08:50 A CDN configuration change (cache key normalisation) is applied by the platform team. This change turned out to be unrelated; see the note at the end.
- 09:12 Deployment of ledger-api 4.18.0 starts. The canary stage routes 5% of traffic to the new build. Migration 0472 runs at 09:13 and completes in 40 seconds.
- 09:20 The deployment automation promotes the canary to 100% of traffic after the standard 8-minute bake. The canary health check, which only calls /health, reported green throughout.
- 09:26 First automated alert: p99 latency on /invoices/render above 2 seconds for 3 consecutive minutes.
- 09:31 On-call engineer Dana Okafor acknowledges the alert.
- 09:33 First customer-reported ticket reaches support (Lena Baxter's team): "invoice PDFs not loading".
- 09:44 Error rate on /invoices/render reaches 38%, its peak. Dana initially suspects the 08:50 CDN change, because render responses are cached at the edge.
- 09:50 The CDN change is ruled out: bypassing the CDN reproduces the failures directly against the origin.
- 09:58 Dana notices that the slow queries correlate with the 4.18.0 deployment and escalates to Marcus Lindqvist, the database lead.
- 10:15 Marcus identifies the root cause: after migration 0472 the planner chooses a sequential scan on invoice_lines for the render query, because table statistics had not been refreshed since the March bulk import. Explain plans confirm it.
- 10:22 Decision: roll back to 4.17.3 rather than run ANALYZE on the live table under load, since the effect of ANALYZE on the running workload was uncertain and no runbook existed.
- 10:29 Rollback starts.
- 10:37 Rollback completes. Error rate on /invoices/render falls below 0.5% within one minute.
- 10:41 Incident declared resolved. Impact window: 09:26 to 10:37, 71 minutes.
- 14:05 ANALYZE is run on invoice_lines during a low-traffic window. Build 4.18.0 is redeployed at 15:20 without recurrence.

Impact
- 14,600 requests to /invoices/render failed or timed out during the impact window, out of roughly 38,400 requests to that endpoint in the same period.
- 212 of 1,940 active customer accounts made at least one failing request. That is 10.9% of active accounts, hence the Medium impact band.
- Three customers on enterprise SLAs qualified for service credits, totalling $4,150.
- No other endpoint exceeded its error budget. No data was lost or corrupted; every invoice that failed to render was rendered successfully after the rollback.
- Support received 27 tickets attributable to the incident, all closed by 15 July.

Root cause
Migration 0472 added the index invoice_lines_invoice_id_position_idx. Planner statistics on invoice_lines had not been refreshed since a bulk import of 9 million rows in March, so the planner's row estimates were wrong by a factor of roughly 20. With the new index present, the planner switched the render query from an index scan to a sequential scan of the full 41-million-row table. Each render query went from about 12 milliseconds to between 2 and 9 seconds, which exhausted the connection pool and caused the timeouts seen by customers.

Contributing factors
1. The canary health check only exercises /health, so the canary looked healthy while /invoices/render was already slow at 5% of traffic.
2. The 8-minute canary bake is shorter than the time the connection pool took to saturate at 5% of traffic.
3. There is no automatic ANALYZE after migrations that add or drop indexes.
4. There was no runbook describing how to diagnose and mitigate planner regressions, which delayed the rollback decision by several minutes.
5. The stale statistics had been a latent condition since March and were not detected by any monitoring.

What went well
- The alert fired 6 minutes after full promotion and 7 minutes before the first customer ticket.
- The rollback was clean and took 8 minutes from start to finish.
- Customer communications went out at 10:05 using the existing status page.

Action items
- AI-1: Extend the canary health check to include a synthetic request to /invoices/render. Owner: Dana Okafor. Due: 31 July 2026. Status: Done (merged 24 July).
- AI-2: Run ANALYZE automatically after any migration that creates or drops an index. Owner: Marcus Lindqvist. Due: 15 August 2026. Status: Open.
- AI-3: Increase the canary bake time from 8 to 30 minutes for ledger-api. Owner: Ravi Thandeka. Due: 31 July 2026. Status: Open (blocked on a deployment tooling change).
- AI-4: Write a runbook for diagnosing query planner regressions, including when it is safe to run ANALYZE under load. Owner: Marcus Lindqvist. Due: 29 August 2026. Status: Open.
- AI-5: Add a customer communication template for partial-degradation incidents. Owner: Lena Baxter. Due: 24 July 2026. Status: Done.

Note on the CDN change
The 08:50 CDN cache key change was initially suspected because it was the most recent change visible on the platform dashboard. It was ruled out at 09:50 and did not contribute to the incident in any way. It remains in place and needs no follow-up.

Brightwater Labs — Quill product meeting (transcript)
Date: Tuesday 8 September 2026, 10:00 to 10:45. Room: Kestrel. Auto-transcribed, lightly cleaned for readability.
Attendees: Amara Osei (product manager, chair); Ben Kristiansen (engineering lead); Chloe Marchetti (design lead); Dev Ramaswamy (data analyst); Elena Voss (marketing lead); Farid Haddad (support lead).
Agenda: (1) launch date for Shared Notebooks; (2) pricing tier for Shared Notebooks; (3) onboarding redesign; (4) support backlog and staffing.

AMARA: Morning everyone. Four items today and I want us out by quarter to eleven. Item one, the launch date for Shared Notebooks. Ben, where is engineering?
BEN: The feature is code complete as of last Thursday. What's left is the permission edge cases, mostly around removing someone from a notebook they created, and the load test. My proposal is Tuesday 13 October. That gives us two full weeks of load testing. I'd say high confidence on 6 October if we cut the load test short, but I don't love that. On 29 September I'd say low confidence, honestly.
CHLOE: I'd push for 29 September. The design work is done, the beta feedback is good, and every week we wait, the momentum from the Templates launch fades. Templates shipped on 11 August and the sign-up bump from it is already flattening.
DEV: For what it's worth, the beta numbers are solid. We have 1,840 beta users on Shared Notebooks, and 62% of them are weekly active. Sharing is the top feature by usage among beta users, ahead of Templates.
ELENA: Marketing needs at least three weeks from a fixed date to prepare the announcement, the email sequence and the partner posts. 29 September is impossible for us. 6 October works if the date is locked today. 13 October is fine too but I'd rather not slide into the conference week.
AMARA: Ben, if we lock 6 October today, can you still do the full load test?
BEN: If we start the load test this Thursday instead of next Monday, yes. Fine, 6 October works. High confidence on that.
CHLOE: I can live with 6 October.
FARID: Support is fine with any of them as long as the help articles are ready a week before.
AMARA: Any objections to Tuesday 6 October? None. Decision: Shared Notebooks launches on Tuesday 6 October. Ben, I need the rollout plan, including the feature flag ramp, by Friday.
BEN: Friday 11 September, done.

AMARA: Item two, pricing. Two options on the table: include Shared Notebooks in the Pro tier at no extra cost, or sell it as a four-dollar-a-month add-on on top of Pro.
ELENA: Add-on. It's our best chance to lift revenue per user this year. My model says about $180,000 in the first twelve months from the add-on alone.
DEV: I looked at the survey from the beta. The people who said they would pay for it were almost all already on Pro. My estimate is that an add-on would be bought by roughly 9% of Pro users, so I get closer to $110,000, and that's before churn from people who feel nickel-and-dimed.
FARID: From the support side an add-on creates a whole class of "why can't I share this notebook" tickets. We saw exactly that with the storage add-on last year; it was about a fifth of our volume for two months.
BEN: No engineering opinion. Both options are the same amount of work, the entitlement check is one line either way.
CHLOE: Design prefers included. The empty state for a locked feature is always ugly.
AMARA: I'm going to decide. Include it in Pro. The retention argument wins over the revenue argument this year; we need Pro to feel complete before the price review in January.
ELENA: I want it on record that I think this is a mistake. We're leaving money on the table and we'll regret it at the January review.
AMARA: Noted, and it will be in the minutes. Decision: Shared Notebooks is included in Pro, no add-on. Elena, I still need the launch announcement draft by 25 September.
ELENA: You'll have it by the 25th.

AMARA: Item three, the onboarding redesign. Chloe?
CHLOE: I'm not ready to present. The user interviews finished on Friday, twelve of them, but I've only synthesised about half. I don't want to show a half picture and have us make decisions on it.
AMARA: Fair. Then we postpone this item to next week's meeting, Tuesday 15 September. Chloe, can you have the research synthesis finished by Monday the 14th so people can read it beforehand?
CHLOE: Yes, by the 14th. I'll circulate it Monday morning.
DEV: If it helps, I can pull the onboarding funnel numbers for the last quarter to go with it.
CHLOE: Please, thanks.

AMARA: Item four, support backlog. Farid.
FARID: The backlog is bad. We have 312 open tickets, median first response time is 31 hours, and the target is 8 hours. I need a contractor for at least three months, ideally starting before the launch.
AMARA: 312? That's almost double last month.
FARID: Sorry, let me correct that. I transposed the digits. It's 213, not 312. Still up from 160 last month, so the trend is the same, but 213 is the right number.
AMARA: OK, 213. Agreed on the contractor anyway; a launch on top of that backlog is not survivable. Can you post the role by Thursday?
FARID: Thursday 10 September, yes.
ELENA: Are launch-day tickets going to be counted in the backlog target? The Templates launch added about 90 tickets in its first week.
FARID: Yes, and that's exactly why I want the contractor in place before 6 October.
AMARA: Dev, can we get a dashboard for shared-notebook adoption before launch?
DEV: It's already live; I built it during the beta. I'll send the link after the meeting. No action needed on my side.

AMARA: Wrap-up. Action items as I have them. Ben: rollout plan by Friday 11 September. Chloe: onboarding research synthesis by Monday 14 September. Elena: launch announcement draft by 25 September. Farid: contractor posting by Thursday 10 September. Me: book the 15 September meeting and circulate these notes today. Dev has no actions.
DEV: Correct, nothing for me.
AMARA: Decisions: launch 6 October; Shared Notebooks included in Pro; onboarding redesign postponed to 15 September; contractor approved for support. Thanks all, that's 10:44.

Millbrook Hollow council adopts $148.6 million budget for 2027 after split vote
By the Millbrook Hollow Ledger staff — published Wednesday 16 September 2026

The Millbrook Hollow town council voted 7 to 2 on Tuesday evening to adopt a $148.6 million operating budget for fiscal year 2027, ending a six-week process that drew larger public turnout than any budget hearing in the past decade. The budget takes effect on 1 January 2027.

The 2027 total is 4.2% higher than the $142.6 million budget adopted for 2026, which in turn had grown from $138.0 million in 2025. Officials said the increase is driven mainly by road maintenance, a new police contract, and higher health insurance costs for town employees.

The council has nine members. The two votes against came from Councillor Ruben Castellanos of Ward 4 and Councillor Anita Reyes of Ward 6. Both said their objection was to a single line item: a 6% cut to the library system, which drops from $5.4 million to $5.1 million.

"I could not vote for a budget that asks the library to do more with less in the same year we add to almost every other department," Councillor Castellanos said after the vote. "The library is the one building in this town that is open to everyone for free. Cutting it by six percent to fund roads is the wrong trade, and I said so at the hearing and I'm saying it again tonight."

Mayor Delphine Aurelio, who presented the budget in August, defended the overall package. "This budget keeps our reserves healthy, funds the road programme residents have been demanding for years, and honours the police contract we negotiated in the spring," she said. "On the library, we are talking about a reduction that comes almost entirely from deferring the branch renovation, not from hours or staff. Nobody is losing a job and no branch is closing."

How the budget was built
The mayor's office released its draft on 4 August, and the council held three work sessions in late August before the public hearing. The draft was $149.1 million; the council trimmed $0.5 million from administration and consulting before Tuesday's vote. Health insurance premiums for the town's 610 employees rose 9% for 2027, adding about $1.9 million across all departments, an increase the council had no power to negotiate this year.

Where the money goes
The largest single allocation is the police department at $41.2 million, or 27.7% of the total, up from $39.0 million in 2026. The increase reflects the three-year contract ratified in April, which raises officer pay by 3.5% a year.

Roads and public works receive $18.9 million, up from $16.9 million, the largest percentage increase of any department. The money funds the resurfacing of 22 miles of town roads, about twice the usual annual programme, and the replacement of the Ferris Creek culvert.

Parks and recreation are flat at $7.4 million. The fire department receives $24.6 million, up 2.1%. Administration, planning and all other departments account for the remaining $51.4 million.

Property taxes
To fund the budget, the property tax rate rises 1.8%. For the owner of a home at the town's median assessed value of $312,000, the increase amounts to about $96 a year, or $8 a month. Sewer and water fees are set separately by the utility board and are not part of Tuesday's vote.

Reserves
The budget leaves the town's general reserve fund at $22.0 million, which is 14.8% of the operating budget. The council's own financial policy, adopted in 2019, requires the reserve to be kept at a minimum of 12% of the operating budget.

"We are comfortably above the policy floor," said Finance Director Margit Halloran, who has held the post since 2021. "Fourteen point eight percent gives us roughly seven weeks of operating expenses in the bank. Two years ago we were at 11.5%, below the floor, and rebuilding that cushion was one of the reasons the 2026 budget was so tight. I would not recommend spending it down to fund the library restoration that some residents asked for; that would be a one-year fix to a recurring cost."

Public hearing
The hearing on 8 September drew about 140 residents to the council chamber, with overflow seating in the lobby. Twenty-three residents spoke. Fifteen of them opposed the library cut, five spoke in favour of the roads programme, and three raised unrelated matters, including a request for a crosswalk on Alder Street. The council did not amend the budget after the hearing.

Water treatment plant
Separately, the council voted unanimously on Tuesday to place a $30 million bond measure for a new water treatment plant on the ballot for the May 2027 election. If approved by voters, the plant would be financed over 25 years and its debt service would appear in the 2028 budget at the earliest. The bond is not part of the $148.6 million operating budget adopted on Tuesday, and the two votes were taken separately.

What happens next
Department heads will submit spending plans by 15 November. The council's finance committee, chaired by Councillor Reyes, will review the library allocation again in the mid-year budget review in June 2027. Councillor Castellanos has said he will propose restoring the library funding at that review if revenue comes in above forecast.

Correction, 17 September 2026: An earlier version of this article stated that the roads and public works allocation increased by 12% from 2026. The correct figure is 11.8%. The earlier version also misspelled the Finance Director's surname as "Halloway"; her name is Margit Halloran. We regret the errors.

Tidewatch backup client — release notes, versions 3.1 to 3.4, followed by the current bug report queue
Severity tags used in these notes: [critical] = crash or data loss; [major] = a feature does not work as documented; [minor] = cosmetic or workaround available.

Version 3.1 — released 12 February 2026
New
- Scheduled backups: choose hourly, daily or weekly schedules per backup set.
- Incremental snapshots: after the first full backup, only changed blocks are uploaded.
- New target types: local folder, network share, and FTP server.
Known issues
- KI-1 (tracked as TW-1099) [major]: files larger than 4 GB fail to back up when the source is on a legacy filesystem such as FAT32; the client reports error E-417. Workaround: move the files to a modern filesystem before backing up.

Version 3.2 — released 9 April 2026
Fixed
- TW-1187 [critical]: the client crashed when a network drive used as a backup source was disconnected during a backup. The backup now pauses and resumes when the drive returns.
- TW-1203 [minor]: log timestamps were written in UTC but labelled as local time.
New
- Bandwidth throttle: limit upload speed per backup set, in MB/s.
- Restore preview: see which files a restore would overwrite before confirming.
Known issues
- KI-1 (TW-1099) [major]: still present; files over 4 GB on legacy filesystems fail with E-417.
- KI-2 (tracked as TW-1240) [major]: the bandwidth throttle setting is not saved across a restart of the client; after a restart the throttle silently reverts to unlimited. Workaround: re-enter the throttle value after each restart.

Version 3.3 — released 2 June 2026
Fixed
- TW-1240 [major]: the bandwidth throttle value is now persisted and survives restarts. This closes KI-2.
- TW-1251 [minor]: the progress bar could stay at 99% for several minutes after the backup had actually completed.
New
- Encryption at rest: an option to encrypt backup sets with a user-held passphrase before upload. Off by default; enabling it on an existing backup set forces a new full backup.
Changed
- Minimum supported operating system version raised; see the compatibility page.
Known issues
- KI-1 (TW-1099) [major]: still present in 3.3; files over 4 GB on legacy filesystems fail with E-417.

Version 3.4 — released 21 August 2026
Fixed
- TW-1099 [major]: files larger than 4 GB on legacy filesystems (FAT32 and similar) are now backed up correctly by splitting them into 2 GB chunks. This closes KI-1, which had been open since 3.1.
- TW-1302 [minor]: restoring a backup set that contained empty folders did not recreate the empty folders.
Deprecated
- The FTP target type is deprecated as of 3.4. It still works in 3.4 and shows a deprecation warning when selected. It will be removed in version 4.0. Users are advised to migrate FTP targets to a network share.
Known issues
- TW-1310 [minor]: when encryption at rest is enabled, the first full backup of a set takes up to 30% longer than an unencrypted full backup. Subsequent incremental backups are not affected. No fix is scheduled yet.

Upgrade notes
- Upgrading from any 3.x version keeps existing backup sets, schedules and targets. The client will ask to re-enter the passphrase for encrypted sets after upgrading to 3.4.
- Downgrading from 3.4 to 3.3 is supported, but any file that was backed up in 2 GB chunks by 3.4 cannot be restored by 3.3.
- Each release is offered through the in-app updater roughly one week after the dates above; the direct download is available on the release date.

Support notes
- Users on 3.1 or 3.2 are advised to upgrade directly to 3.4; there is no need to install 3.3 first.
- Version 3.0 and earlier are out of support since 30 June 2026.

BUG REPORT QUEUE (as of 10 September 2026)

BR-1 — submitted 15 May 2026 — reporter running version 3.2
"I set the upload throttle to 2 MB/s on my main backup set. Every time I reboot my computer the throttle goes back to unlimited and my video calls stutter during the morning backup. I have to set it again every day."
Triage note: matches KI-2 / TW-1240. Fixed in 3.3. Reporter advised to upgrade. Status: closed as fixed.

BR-2 — submitted 3 July 2026 — reporter running version 3.3
"Backups of my 6 GB video project file fail with error E-417 every time. The file is on an old external drive formatted FAT32. Smaller files on the same drive back up fine."
Triage note: matches KI-1 / TW-1099, which was still open when this report was submitted. Fixed in 3.4 (released 21 August). Reporter notified on 22 August. Status: closed as fixed.

BR-3 — submitted 30 August 2026 — reporter running version 3.4
"Since I turned on encryption at rest, the first backup took about 30% longer than my previous full backup of the same folder. Later incremental backups seem normal. Is this expected?"
Triage note: matches known issue TW-1310, which is documented in the 3.4 notes and has no scheduled fix. Status: open, linked to TW-1310.

BR-4 — submitted 20 May 2026 — reporter running version 3.2
"The bandwidth limit doesn't stick. I put in 5 MB/s, close the app, open it again, and it's gone."
Triage note: duplicate of BR-1 (same underlying issue, KI-2 / TW-1240). Fixed in 3.3. Status: closed as duplicate of BR-1.

Queue summary: four reports; two closed as fixed, one closed as duplicate, one open.
